name: Copenhagen
operatingHours: Metro lines M1, M2, M3 (Cityringen) and M4 run 24/7: every 2–4 min by day and ~every 7–15 min late at night. S-tog suburban trains (not on this map) stop around 1 AM on weekdays with night service Fri–Sat.
fareInfo: Zone-based tickets, from ~DKK 24 for 2 zones (2026); the airport is zone 4. A 24-hour City Pass (zones 1–4, incl. airport) is ~DKK 80 and a 72-hour one ~DKK 200. Buy in the DOT Tickets app, at machines or tap with a Rejsekort; check in before boarding.

lines.name: M2
lines.firstLast: Airport (Lufthavnen) ↔ Kongens Nytorv: 24 hours, every 4–20 min, ~15 min.

sights.name: Nyhavn
sights.note: The 17th-century canal harbour lined with colourful townhouses, wooden ships and cafés; the classic Copenhagen postcard.

sights.name: Tivoli Gardens
sights.note: Historic amusement park and garden in the city centre, with rides, concerts and lights after dark. Seasonal: summer, Halloween and Christmas openings only.
sights.hours: Seasonal: ~11:00 AM–10 or 11 PM in open periods; closed between seasons (check dates)

sights.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
sights.note: Art museum with a large antiquities collection and French Impressionists, built around a glass-domed winter garden.
sights.hours: 11:00 AM–6:00 PM, till 10:00 PM Thu, closed Mon

sights.name: Rosenborg Castle
sights.note: Renaissance royal castle of Christian IV housing the crown jewels and royal regalia, set in the King's Garden.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–4:00 PM daily in autumn (longer in summer, shorter in winter; check)

sights.name: Torvehallerne
sights.note: Two glass halls of food stalls: smørrebrød, seafood, pastries, coffee and Danish produce next to Nørreport.
sights.hours: Mon–Thu ~10:00 AM–7:00 PM, Fri till 8:00 PM, Sat till 6:00 PM, Sun till 5:00 PM

sights.name: Christiansborg Palace
sights.note: Seat of the Danish parliament, with royal reception rooms, ruins beneath the palace and a tower with a free city view.
sights.hours: Royal rooms and ruins ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Tue–Sun in winter; tower Tue–Sun

sights.name: The National Museum of Denmark
sights.note: Danish history from the Stone Age and Vikings to modern times, plus a lively children's museum.

sights.name: The Round Tower (Rundetaarn)
sights.note: Seventeenth-century observatory tower reached by a spiral ramp, with a rooftop view over the old town.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM daily (till 8:00 PM in summer)

sights.name: Our Saviour's Church
sights.note: Baroque church whose corkscrew spire has an external staircase to the top, with a view over Christianshavn.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM daily; tower closed in ice or high wind

sights.name: Copenhagen Botanical Garden
sights.note: University botanical garden with a Victorian palm house, rock garden and lake; the garden itself is free.
sights.hours: Garden from ~8:30 AM to ~4:00 PM in autumn/winter (later in summer); glasshouses ~10:00 AM–4:00 PM

sights.name: Amalienborg Palace
sights.note: Residence of the royal family around an octagonal square, with a museum of royal rooms and a daily changing of the guard at noon.
sights.hours: Museum ~10:00 AM–4:00 PM (closed Mon in winter); guard change 12:00 noon

sights.name: Strøget
sights.note: One of Europe's longest pedestrian shopping streets, running from the City Hall Square toward Kongens Nytorv.

sights.name: Home of Carlsberg
sights.note: Visitor centre at the original Carlsberg brewery, with the history of beer-making, the stables and tastings.

sights.name: Copenhagen Opera House
sights.note: Waterfront opera house by Henning Larsen on Holmen island; best seen by attending a performance or a guided tour.
sights.hours: Performance and tour times vary (check); not open for free walk-in visits

sights.name: Freetown Christiania
sights.note: Self-governing alternative community in former military barracks, with murals, workshops and cafés. Photography is not allowed on Pusher Street; be respectful.

sights.name: Frederik's Church (Marble Church)
sights.note: Baroque-style marble church with Northern Europe's largest dome, next to Amalienborg.
sights.hours: Mon–Thu 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Fri–Sun noon–5:00 PM

sights.name: The David Collection
sights.note: Free museum of Islamic art, European 18th-century decorative art and early Danish silver in a townhouse overlooking the King's Garden.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM, closed Mon; free entry

sights.name: The King's Garden (Kongens Have)
sights.note: Copenhagen's oldest royal park, with lawns, rose garden and summer picnics around Rosenborg Castle. A local-flavour addition.

railStations.name: Copenhagen Central Station
railStations.note: Main station (København H), beside Tivoli: DSB intercity trains to Aarhus, Odense and Malmö (Sweden, ~35 min) and S-tog suburban trains. M3 and M4 metro lines stop at København H beneath it.
railStations.hours: Trains run ~5:00 AM–1:00 AM; some night services Fri–Sat. Metro 24/7.

airports.name: Copenhagen Airport
airports.transitNote: The Airport station on the M2 metro line (shown on this map) reaches Kongens Nytorv in ~15 min and Nørreport in ~17 min; trains also run direct to Central Station in ~13 min (DSB/Øresundståg, not the metro).
airports.hours: Metro M2: 24/7, every ~4–6 min by day, ~every 15 min late at night.
